title: Shepherd's Pie
shortDescription: Golden potato cap over rich filling, Greek salad on the side
subtitle: Golden potato cap over rich filling, Greek salad on the side
description: Golden potato cap over rich filling, Greek salad on the side

steps.title: Brown the filling
steps.instruction: Brown ground lamb with diced onion until deeply colored. Drain excess fat. Add peas, carrots, broth, and tomato paste; simmer 15 minutes until thick.

steps.title: Mash the topping
steps.instruction: Boil russets until tender; mash with butter and cream until smooth. Season with salt and white pepper.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.instruction: Spread filling in hotel pans; pipe or spread mashed potatoes over top. Fork ridges for crispy peaks. Bake at 400°F 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling at edges.

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes so filling sets — scoops stay clean on the line. Shepherd's Pie feeds a hall that wants something hearty after a cold call.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Shepherd's Pie with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Shepherd's Pie on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Golden potato cap over rich filling, Greek salad on the side. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
